title: The domestic church (Lumen Gentium 11)
hook: parents as first teachers of faith at home
tomorrow: is holiness only for nuns and saints in stained glass?

segments.voice: Last week closed on the first lines of Lumen Gentium: Christ the light, and the Church like a sacrament, a sign for all. Same document, ten paragraphs on, and a lot closer to home.

The rice is boiling over. The math worksheet is half done. And a seven-year-old, mid-bite, looks up and asks: where does God live? Every grown-up at the table goes quiet. Nobody in that kitchen is ordained. There's no altar and no bell, just a pot lid rattling, and the parish office is closed till Monday. Somebody has to say something. Vatican II's document on the Church has a name for that kitchen, and a job description for whoever answers.
screen: `WHERE DOES GOD LIVE?` → `NOBODY HERE IS ORDAINED.` → `SOMEBODY HAS TO ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Paragraph eleven of Lumen Gentium walks through the sacraments one by one, showing how the whole people of God lives its faith. When it reaches marriage, it slows down. First, the couple. Christian spouses, it says, are a sign of the unity and fruitful love between Christ and the Church, and they help each other toward holiness, in married life and in raising children. Second, the family that grows from them: children born into human society, and through baptism made children of God. Third, the name. The family, the council says, is, so to speak, the domestic church. Notice the hedge: so to speak. A home isn't a parish. But something of the Church truly happens there. Fourth, the job description. In this domestic church, parents are to be the first heralds of the faith to their children, by word and by example. First, before the catechist, before the priest. And the paragraph adds that parents should encourage each child in the calling that is truly that child's own. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the council didn't put the first teacher of faith in a pulpit. It put that teacher at the dinner table, often with a pot boiling over.
screen: `THE COUPLE: A SIGN OF CHRIST'S LOVE.` · `THE FAMILY: CHILDREN OF GOD.` · `THE NAME: SO TO SPEAK, A CHURCH.` · `THE JOB: FIRST HERALDS OF FAITH.` · then, large: `THE CHURCH AT HOME.`

segments.voice: If someone you live with is nearby, invite them into this quiet, and say aloud together a grace some Catholic families say at meals: Bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts, which we are about to receive from thy bounty, through Christ our Lord. Amen. If you're alone, say the names of the people you call family, by blood or by choice, one name to a breath.
The domestic church. Lumen Gentium's so-to-speak name for a family: the place faith is first heard and seen.
Your line: the church at home. It meets wherever the first questions get asked. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1583 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: IS HOLINESS ONLY FOR NUNS AND SAINTS?`

howItsDone: In Catholic homes, families may say grace at meals, pray together at bedtime, keep a crucifix or a small prayer corner, and bless their children; parishes speak of parents as their children's first teachers in faith.

fork.setup: your neighbor, dad of twins, says he's "not religious enough" to teach them anything about God, so he'll leave it to religious ed. what does Lumen Gentium 11 say to him?
options: wait: first teaching belongs to trained catechists.
study theology first, then start teaching them.
he's a first herald, by word and by example.
fork.reveal: the council calls parents the first heralds of the faith to their children, by word and example, in the family it calls the domestic church. no degree required.

chat.says: watching my cousin Lupe for two weeks while tía works nights. she asked where God lives. do i answer?
options: Answer her simply. The council calls home a domestic church, where faith is first passed on.
Leave it for her mom or for Sunday school. They're the ones trained to teach this stuff.
Tell her it's a grown-up question. Kids are better off waiting until they're older.
chat.meaning: Lumen Gentium 11 calls the family, so to speak, the domestic church: faith is first heard at home, by word and example.

Lumen Gentium.meaning: Vatican II's document on the Church; Latin for light of the nations

Vatican II.meaning: the Second Vatican Council, a gathering of the world's Catholic bishops

ordained.meaning: made a deacon, priest or bishop through holy orders

heralds.meaning: people who announce news; here, who first proclaim the faith

catechist.meaning: someone who teaches the faith in a parish or school

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church

notes: Lumen Gentium 11 paraphrased (official English not public domain): confirm the walk through the sacraments, spouses signifying the mystery of unity and fruitful love between Christ and the Church, helping each other to holiness, children made children of God by baptism, 'the family is, so to speak, the domestic church', parents as 'the first preachers (heralds) of the faith' by word and example, and encouraging each child's proper vocation (the text adds special care for a sacred vocation; omitted for length).
Original game: 'Ecclesia domestica' as in LG 11's Latin (velut Ecclesia domestica); confirm.
